notes: This file stress-tests Activity with realistic quiet-period monitoring volume.
All entries are sanitized representative observations, not canonical database facts.
Quiet entries should not become Home noise by default.

alerts.title: Ticketed play announcement would open planning mode
alerts.summary: When Atlanta ticketed play goes live, Home should announce it and Explore becomes the triage lane for event comparison.
alerts.rationale: This is the highest-value quiet-period signal because ticketed play changes the app from watch mode into planning mode.
alerts.nextAction: If observed live, show on Home, add a Calendar milestone, and open Explore with Play selected.

alerts.title: Black Lotus page changes are big by default
alerts.summary: The VIP page controls First Look, included events, store entitlement, pickup, and logistics, so meaningful edits stay high-signal.
alerts.rationale: Kavi and Chris have Black Lotus badges; Juan does not. Changes here have direct planning and retrieval value.
alerts.nextAction: Escalate material changes to Home unless clearly cosmetic; preserve old and new source wording in Activity.

alerts.title: Atlanta site tree is watched beyond the home page
alerts.summary: New, removed, renamed, or materially changed official Atlanta pages can hydrate Activity instead of relying on manual page patrol.
alerts.rationale: Prior MagicCon surfaces show that maps, app links, artists, store, prize wall, and operational details often land as page updates.
alerts.nextAction: Route meaningful page changes to Home plus Activity with exact URL, useful wording, and affected destination.

alerts.title: Artist directory belongs in Artists when it appears
alerts.summary: The first official artist list should become a browsable opportunity surface, not just a flat copied directory.
alerts.rationale: Artist info is valuable when the app translates it into lazy-friendly signature/card opportunities.
alerts.nextAction: Show first appearance on Home; later changes stay in Activity unless they match known card/signature interest.

alerts.title: Show store catalog should become a retrieval tool
alerts.summary: When the official catalog appears, it should be over-ingested into searchable items with favorites, ignored items, and receipt backlinks.
alerts.rationale: Store info is annoying to find onsite and becomes more useful inside the app than in the canonical source.
alerts.nextAction: Route first catalog appearance to Home; put item-level extraction and assignment context in Wallet and Activity.

alerts.title: Prize wall belongs with Wallet and onsite refresh
alerts.summary: Prize wall availability matters mostly during the event, especially because stock can sell out and later refresh.
alerts.rationale: Prize Tix only become decision-useful if available prizes can be compared against the wallet total.
alerts.nextAction: When official inventory appears, link Prize Tix balance to prize browsing without making the counter itself complicated.

alerts.title: Official map lands in Map, then backlinks outward
alerts.summary: Official 2026 floor artifacts should attach to Map and become useful through room, booth, vendor, Wallet, and event backlinks.
alerts.rationale: The map is valuable when it helps answer where to go next rather than simply reproducing a giant image.
alerts.nextAction: Keep first official map as a Home signal; put extraction and OCR candidates in Map/Activity for review.

alerts.title: Official app link is worth noticing once published
alerts.summary: A MagicCon app download link can become another source for maps, schedules, vendors, notifications, and onsite logistics.
alerts.rationale: The app may contain useful operational data even if it is clunky as the primary interface.
alerts.nextAction: Keep as Activity unless it unlocks map, ticketed play, schedule, or vendor data.

alerts.title: Vendor exclusives need a low-noise radar lane
alerts.summary: Dragon Shield-style exclusive merch is worth surfacing when a vendor or official source makes it concrete.
alerts.rationale: This is a good AI value-add if it finds real exclusive items without spamming vague hype.
alerts.nextAction: Keep radar leads in Activity/Explore until confirmed by first-party source or inbox evidence.

alerts.title: Receipt imports should be quiet unless action is needed
alerts.summary: MagicCon receipts belong in Wallet with original proof, extracted line items, quantities, assignments, and catalog backlinks.
alerts.rationale: Receipts are valuable retrieval objects but usually not news.
alerts.nextAction: Store full artifacts only after private Storage is designed; keep public preview entries sanitized.

alerts.title: Ticketed-play receipts deserve a high-utility Wallet lane
alerts.summary: Play receipts can carry event codes, pickup proof, and original receipt images that may need to be shown onsite.
alerts.rationale: Play receipts are more operational than ordinary receipts because they can affect check-in or event pickup.
alerts.nextAction: Route to Wallet Play with QR/code popovers, original receipt preview, and object backlinks.

alerts.title: Hotel confirmations stay useful but quiet
alerts.summary: Hotel emails should hydrate Trip with address, dates, people, links, and check-in/out times without becoming Home clutter.
alerts.rationale: The value is pleasant retrieval and transition context, not proving that Kavi has a hotel.
alerts.nextAction: Escalate only if a hotel email changes timing, property, cancellation, or payment status.

alerts.title: Delta changes stay under Trip unless timing breaks
alerts.summary: Flight-time changes should annotate Trip and Calendar; only meaningful disruption reaches Home.
alerts.rationale: Trip should be a pleasant reference and change surface, not a full flight-monitoring product.
alerts.nextAction: Escalate only if departure, arrival, check-in, lodging, or event timing is materially affected.

alerts.title: Generic MagicCon newsletter stays out of Home
alerts.summary: A general MagicCon post with no Atlanta planning unlock should be recorded only as source history.
alerts.rationale: Quiet checks are confidence-building evidence, not engagement material.
alerts.nextAction: Keep reviewed in Sources; do not publish a preview only for this kind of result.

alerts.title: Pastimes format resources support complexity labels
alerts.summary: Format explanations can help translate weird event listings, but they should not become standalone alerts.
alerts.rationale: This supports event-detail AI value without pretending every glossary page is news.
alerts.nextAction: Use when ticketed-play data creates demand for a source-backed format registry.

alerts.title: Leap schedule placeholder should be checked carefully
alerts.summary: The eventual ticketed-play surface may first appear as a sparse or placeholder page before real inventory lands.
alerts.source: Leap Conventions / leapevent with MagicCon context
alerts.rationale: The query must be MagicCon-specific; standalone Leap is too broad and noisy.
alerts.nextAction: Escalate only when Atlanta event inventory, sellout state, or registration timing appears.

alerts.title: Badge shipping and badge proof belong in Wallet
alerts.summary: Badge-related emails should attach to Wallet as proof and logistics, with no privacy-sensitive codes in public preview.
alerts.rationale: Badges are operationally important onsite, but most badge emails are retrieval facts rather than Home alerts.
alerts.nextAction: Escalate only for missing badge, shipping issue, or pickup requirement.

alerts.title: Meet-and-greet wristbands are a special opportunity class
alerts.summary: If wristbands or limited sessions appear, they should surface as time-sensitive opportunities rather than generic news.
alerts.rationale: These can disappear quickly and may affect day planning without being ticketed play.
alerts.nextAction: Route first appearance to Home if action timing matters; otherwise keep in Explore/Activity.

alerts.title: Black Lotus store email should break through
alerts.summary: The early online store window can be janky and inventory-sensitive, so the app should treat a real store-opening email as urgent.
alerts.rationale: Stuff can sell out quickly and the entitlement may only be usable once.
alerts.nextAction: Show on Home, attach to Wallet/Store, and preserve useful source wording without exposing private links publicly.

alerts.title: Deadlines and travel anchors belong in Calendar
alerts.summary: Non-event dates such as check-in, checkout, flight time, leave-for-airport, and purchase deadlines should be visible in the agenda stream.
alerts.rationale: Calendar is the broad date stream; Plan is reserved for convention-day contention.
alerts.nextAction: Use Calendar for dated anchors and Plan only when event-resource contention needs the detailed view.
